A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SFLCB research work and contain 41 pages, including appendices A–F. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the scientific content, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original SFLCB experiments on a toy problem, diabetes-dataset SVM hyperparameter optimization, and transportation network design, including sensitivity results. Appendix F documents experimental settings.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and results in Section 6, including the sensitivity analysis, with their settings in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The penalty and augmented-Lagrangian reformulation, SFLCB components, and Algorithm 1 update rules are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same toy problem, diabetes-dataset SVM task, and synthetic transportation networks with 3 and 9 nodes.

E2.justification: The SVM comparison retains GAM, LV-HBA, BLOCC, and BiC-GAFFA; the transportation comparison retains BLOCC. Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain identical experimental formulations, regularization, optimization budgets, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The toy experiment with 200 initializations and the transportation sensitivity analysis over five delta values are unchanged. No ablations or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report SVM averages and one standard deviation over 10 random splits, and sensitivity-analysis averages and one standard deviation over three random seeds.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 are visually identical, retaining the same toy solutions, SVM accuracy curves, transportation utilities, and sensitivity results. The accompanying numerical statements and findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, reformulation guarantees, convergence statements, and supporting derivations and proofs in appendices A–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reformulation accuracy, the single-loop first-order algorithm, convergence complexity, and practical efficiency.

C2.justification: The interpretation of delta's convergence–approximation tradeoff and the stated limitations to deterministic, linearly constrained settings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains identical implementation information, hardware descriptions, and hyperparameters. The simulation-code access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 53 cited works with unchanged bibliographic content and research positioning. Reference entries move between pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: The acknowledgement replaces Jiawei Zhang's university startup-funding description with support through UW–Madison's Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Graduate Education, funded by the Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgement causes reference spacing and page breaks to change on pages 11–14; the first-page arXiv stamp also updates. The scientific figures, table, algorithm display, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides more specific funding attribution and reflows the bibliography. The scientific exposition, proofs, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so these administrative and layout edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
